authors: Alfons van Marrewijk, Stewart R. Clegg, Tyrone S. Pitsis, Marcel Veenswijk
method: comparative ethnographic case study (Environ, NL; NSTP, Sydney 2000)
definition: No project-governance definition. PPP = 'structural cooperation between public and private parties to deliver some agreed outcome' (p. 591).
stakeholders: Public + private partners; politicians. Environ: EUR800m overrun -> parliamentary inquiry -> politicians demand control -> ministry centralization. NSTP: no-blame alliance culture resolves conflict.
decision_making: Yes (Brief) - comparative case analysis; alliance vs concession decision structures.
temporality_detail: Decade-long PPP phases; political interference framed as disruption to design/culture. No cyclical/electoral clock.
megaproject_detail: Two PPP megaprojects (Environ NL; North Side Tunnel Project, Sydney 2000 Olympics).
misalignment_detail: Political takeover after overrun is a political-time analogue at cabinet scale, but explained via project design/culture, not temporal mismatch.
gaps: Rejects Flyvbjerg 'deception' thesis; explains outcomes via design/culture. Establishes design x culture lens the RQ can layer an electoral clock onto; no recurring political clock.
key_quotes: 'structural cooperation between public and private parties to deliver some agreed outcome' (p. 591).
Project design and project cultures 'play a role in determining how managers and partners cooperate' (abstract).
coding_notes: Emic/ethnographic; origin of the widely-cited PPP definition. Clegg co-authors both this and Dille et al. (2018) - cross-reference.

definition: No one-sentence definition; governance of PM = balancing Education / Management Demand / Perceived Economic Pressure.
stakeholders: Sponsor + PMO members; core is the agency problem (weak sponsor vs project manager).
temporality_detail: Pressure 'reduces the time horizon view of the project manager drastically... short-term survival.' No electoral time.
misalignment_detail: Manager-level horizon compression is an analogue; no external clock.
gaps: Extend horizon-compression logic to electoral pressure.
key_quotes: Pressure 'reduces the time horizon view of the project manager drastically... short-term survival.'
coding_notes: Foundational definitional source (controls/processes/relationships lineage). Scanned pagination unreliable - cited by concept.

definition: Governance = 'forms of organization designed ex ante'; governing = 'spontaneous micro-processes... ex post' (p. 432).
elements: three explanation-types (rent-seeking / misaligned governance / diverse cultures, Table 3)
stakeholders: Politicians, contractors, sponsors, participants. Resolution differs per explanation-type.
decision_making: Yes - typology on cognition x view of the future.
temporality_detail: Ex-ante/ex-post is temporal (p. 436); promoters 'often not in office when the actual viability of a project can be assessed... political capital in the short-term.'
misalignment_detail: Electoral-accountability gap named (promoter out of office), framed as rent-seeking rather than recurring misfit.
gaps: Governing-vs-governance is the dynamic lens; electoral timing named but not modelled.
key_quotes: Governance = 'forms of organization designed ex ante'; governing = 'spontaneous micro-processes... ex post' (p. 432).
Promoters 'often not in office when the actual viability of a project can be assessed... political capital in the short-term' (p. 436).
coding_notes: Esposito & Terlizzi (2023) build directly on this governance/governing distinction - cross-reference.

method: comparative case (San Francisco vs Map Ta Phut)
definition: Polycentric governance = 'multiple independent actors mutually order their relationships... under a general system of rules' (V. Ostrom).
stakeholders: Govt + private + civil society coordinate 'around the agenda, not a hegemonic body'; partisan mutual adjustment.
temporality_detail: 'polycentricity as a dynamic process, not an event'; path dependency. No electoral cycle.
misalignment_detail: Models polycentric order as stable; electoral clock could perturb it.
gaps: Strongest 'coordination across levels' treatment; no electoral clock.
key_quotes: Polycentric governance = 'multiple independent actors mutually order their relationships... under a general system of rules' (V. Ostrom).
coding_notes: Scanned/preprint pagination unreliable - cited by concept.

authors: Tuomas Ahola, Inkeri Ruuska, Karlos Artto, Jaakko Kujala
definition: Two streams: external to / internal to a project; 'there is clearly a lack of a shared and universally accepted view of what project governance actually is' (p. 1324).
stakeholders: External: project-based firm vs project (agency). Internal: multiple firms with conflicting short/long-term goals + shared mechanisms.
temporality_detail: Governance as 'continuous... process' vs 'relatively static set of mechanisms' (pp. 1323-24); public projects tied to 'political processes that are dynamic and often difficult to predict' (p. 1325).
misalignment_detail: Flags political-process unpredictability and static-vs-dynamic debate; no electoral model.
gaps: Frames the static-vs-dynamic governance question the RQ inherits.
key_quotes: 'there is clearly a lack of a shared and universally accepted view of what project governance actually is' (p. 1324).
Governance as 'continuous... process' vs 'relatively static set of mechanisms' (pp. 1323-24).
coding_notes: The external/internal cut is the field's organizing frame; cited by Bakhshi (2025), Pathak (2023).

definition: Turner (2009, p. 311): governance 'provides the structure through which the objectives... are set, and the means of attaining... and monitoring performance are determined.'
stakeholders: Sponsor, owner, principal/agent, steward; theory-dependent resolution.
temporality_detail: Short vs long horizons; life cycle. No external clock.
misalignment_detail: Level scaffolding only; no electoral clock.
gaps: Provides the multi-level scaffolding on which cross-level electoral effects act.
key_quotes: Governance 'provides the structure through which the objectives... are set, and the means of attaining... and monitoring performance are determined' (Turner 2009, via Table 2, p. 1294).
coding_notes: Widely cited as the multi-level governance reference (Pathak 2023 builds its multi-level aspect on it).

definition: Project governance = 'the use of systems, structures of authority, and processes to allocate resources and coordinate or control activity in a project' (Pinto 2014, quoted p. 613); 'coexists within the corporate governance framework' (Müller 2009).
elements: governance paradigms: shareholder-stakeholder orientation x behavior-outcome control (Müller & Lecoeuvre 2014)
stakeholders: Parent organization over project; more shareholder- vs more stakeholder-oriented. Finding: success rises with stakeholder orientation; control-type immaterial.
temporality_detail: Cross-sectional; success related to stakeholder orientation at a single point in time. Does not treat temporality/rhythm.
misalignment_detail: Static snapshot; no timing dimension.
gaps: Cements the shareholder<->stakeholder and behavior<->outcome axes and the stewardship result - but static. RQ can ask how an electoral cycle swings a parent between orientations over a project's life.
key_quotes: Project governance = 'the use of systems, structures of authority, and processes to allocate resources and coordinate or control activity in a project' (Pinto 2014, p. 613).
Project success correlates with increasing stakeholder orientation; types of control mechanisms do not correlate (abstract, p. 613).
coding_notes: Empirical anchor for the shareholder/stakeholder axis reused by Gil & Beckman (2025). Müller co-authors items 2, 7, 22 - author cluster.

outlet: Studies of Transition States and Societies 10(1), 3-14
definition: No PG definition. Megaproject = 'very large infrastructure investments... more than US$1 billion' (p. 3).
stakeholders: Political elites decide & legitimate via discourse; civil society opposes. Regime type (democratic alternation vs authoritarian continuity) resolves.
temporality_detail: 'power has changed hands repeatedly in Italy, while Tajikistan has had the same president since 1993... continuity has supported greater progress on the Rogun Dam than the SoMB' (p. 8).
misalignment_detail: Electoral alternation vs continuity determines megaproject fate - via ideology/symbolism, not governance mechanics.
gaps: Demonstrates electoral alternation effect but through ideology, not governance machinery.
key_quotes: Megaproject = 'very large infrastructure investments... more than US$1 billion' (p. 3).
'power has changed hands repeatedly in Italy, while Tajikistan has had the same president since 1993... continuity has supported greater progress on the Rogun Dam' (p. 8).
coding_notes: Cleanest natural experiment on regime alternation vs continuity in the corpus.

authors: Christopher Biesenthal, Stewart Clegg, Ashwin Mahalingam, Shankar Sankaran
definition: No explicit definition - institutional theory. Megaproject via Flyvbjerg (2014, p. 6).
elements: 'polycentric governance structures obfuscate hierarchical decision making' (p. 49)
stakeholders: 'widely disparate actors... conflicting interests'; cognitive conflicts hardest (p. 47); institutional entrepreneurship.
temporality_detail: Duration 'extending beyond the political life cycle of a national government' (p. 45); reverse clocks.
misalignment_detail: Names the duration-vs-political-cycle tension; models it nowhere.
gaps: Names the tension the thesis formalises; no model.
key_quotes: Duration 'extending beyond the political life cycle of a national government' (p. 45).
'polycentric governance structures obfuscate hierarchical decision making' (p. 49).
coding_notes: Clegg co-authors items 1, 9, 10 - author cluster; institutional-theory bridge to Qiu (2019) and Esposito & Terlizzi (2023).

authors: Therese Dille, Jonas Söderlund, Stewart Clegg
method: processual longitudinal case study (Norwegian TETRA emergency network; 40 interviews)
definition: No PG definition. Temporal conditioning = 'the process of responding to and coping with institutionally prescribed and conflicting temporal demands' (p. 673); inter-institutional project.
elements: three strategies: temporal avoidance / splitting / matching
stakeholders: Three emergency services (Health/Fire/Police) with divergent time horizons; DNK project org; government/Parliament as temporal gate; contractor MultiCom. PM team plays constituencies off (temporal matching).
decision_making: Yes - processual analysis of managerial temporal responses across five phases.
temporality_detail: Divergent institutional time-reckoning systems; 'significant temporal misfit across the public subprojects' (p. 678); simultaneous speeding-up/slowing-down; Parliament approval as a temporal gate (Step 1->Step 2). No repeating electoral cycle.
misalignment_detail: The keystone temporal-conditioning machinery: divergent clocks within one project + government/Parliament exogenous temporal gate + three named coping strategies. External gate is a one-off parliamentary vote, not a recurring election.
gaps: Reusable to classify megaproject responses to electoral-temporal misfit; its external gate is one-off, not cyclical.
key_quotes: Temporal conditioning = 'the process of responding to and coping with institutionally prescribed and conflicting temporal demands' (p. 673).
PM team 'was unable to resolve the significant temporal misfit across the public subprojects' (p. 678).
Strategies = 'temporal avoidance', 'temporal splitting', 'temporal matching' (p. 682).
coding_notes: Clegg + Söderlund author cluster (Söderlund also co-authors Ika 2025). Directly instantiates entrainment concepts Ika (2025) later theorizes.

authors: Felipe Livert, Xabier Gainza, Ignacio Acuña
definition: No PG definition - urban/metropolitan governance & distributive politics.
stakeholders: Central govt + mayors; transfers 'used to win, exercise, and retain power' (p. 2). Elected two-tier authority proposed.
temporality_detail: Electoral time, not project time. Political budget cycles (p. 2); tenure (p. 7); fixed electoral calendar.
misalignment_detail: Electoral clock without a project timeline; supplies core/swing & budget-cycle mechanism.
gaps: Has the electoral clock but no project timeline to misalign it against.
key_quotes: Transfers 'used to win, exercise, and retain power' (p. 2).
coding_notes: Political-budget-cycle mechanism; complements project-clock papers.

authors: Yong Qiu, Hongquan Chen, Zhiyong Sheng, Suzhen Cheng
definition: Governance = 'all of the mechanisms within a project organization that... determine how resources are used and distributed... and resolve conflicts' (p. 427).
stakeholders: Four governments + designers/contractors/public; 'system leaders... conflicting buffer' (p. 435).
temporality_detail: Moderate, project-internal. 'evolutionary complexity... dynamic during their entire life cycle' (p. 425).
misalignment_detail: Concurrent-jurisdiction governments, not electorally refreshed.
gaps: Multi-government structure but no electoral turnover modelled.
key_quotes: Governance = 'all of the mechanisms within a project organization that... determine how resources are used and distributed... and resolve conflicts' (p. 427).
'evolutionary complexity... dynamic during their entire life cycle' (p. 425).
coding_notes: Six-complexity typology parallels Esposito & Terlizzi (2023); cited by Pathak (2023).

definition: 'clearly defined governance structure... to organize the inter-organizational relationships between sponsors, clients, delivery partners, and the supply chain' (Exec. Summary).
stakeholders: Sponsor/client/delivery-partner; roles 'nonstatic and evolutionary... throughout the project life cycle.'
temporality_detail: Moderate. Roles 'nonstatic and evolutionary... throughout the project life cycle'; short-term-results tendency.
misalignment_detail: Client-role evolution over life cycle + a government-sponsor node an electoral turnover would disrupt.
gaps: Evolving roles but no external electoral clock.
key_quotes: Roles have a 'nonstatic and evolutionary nature throughout the project life cycle' (Exec. Summary).
coding_notes: PSO framework cited by Pathak (2023).

definition: Governance = 'Framework for managers to do work' vs governmentality = 'the way governors interact with those they govern' (Table 2).
stakeholders: Board sets governmentality; PM sovereignty scale; Amsterdam principal-agency->stewardship shift.
temporality_detail: Governmentality 'changes... from design to execution' (p. 7). No electoral time.
misalignment_detail: Governmentality localises where an election bites; Amsterdam restructuring is an analogue.
gaps: Structure/governmentality split is a key RQ tool; no electoral clock.
key_quotes: Governance = 'Framework for managers to do work'; governmentality = 'the way governors interact with those they govern' (Table 2, p. 4).
coding_notes: Governmentality lens reused by Afieroho (2024).

authors: Tristano Sainati, Giorgio Locatelli, Nigel Smith, Naomi Brookes, Gordon Olver
definition: 'Project governance defines both the organisational structures and processes to govern the project... assigning project roles and responsibilities' (p. 244).
stakeholders: Holders of 'a legal, or contractual, claim'; SPVs cluster stakeholders; lenders control.
temporality_detail: Minimal - SPV 'liquidated when... functions... accomplished' (p. 252). Does not treat temporality.
misalignment_detail: Static architecture; formal-instrument layer only.
gaps: The durable contractual/SPV layer against which cyclical metagovernance could be contrasted.
key_quotes: 'Project governance defines both the organisational structures and processes to govern the project... assigning project roles and responsibilities to project stakeholders' (p. 244).
coding_notes: Represents the static formal-instrument end of the spectrum.

definition: Governance framework (Klakegg et al., 2008: S30): 'an organized structure established as authoritative within the institution, comprising processes and rules established to ensure projects meet their purpose.'
stakeholders: Project actors; ministers/Treasury Board/SQI. Conflict = tensions between objectives/levels.
temporality_detail: Moderate. 'dynamic aspects'; framework evolution over years; 'a project has a political dimension' (p. 410).
misalignment_detail: Legitimacy at political level; election timing not a variable.
gaps: Political dimension acknowledged; electoral timing not modelled.
key_quotes: Governance framework = 'an organized structure established as authoritative within the institution, comprising processes and rules established to ensure projects meet their purpose' (Klakegg et al. 2008, p. 406).
'a project has a political dimension' (p. 410).
coding_notes: Same author as item 25 (Brunet & Choinière 2024), distinct paper; shares the Klakegg definition.

definition: No governance definition. Project narratives = 'coherent, performative narratives that project an intended future' (p. 44).
stakeholders: Champion, team, external stakeholders; 'convincing oneself; the team; stakeholders.'
temporality_detail: Core (theory of project time). Shaping->delivery narratives across the life cycle. No electoral cycle.
misalignment_detail: Narrative/temporal-work apparatus for re-narration under turnover.
gaps: Supplies re-narration machinery; not pointed at elections.
key_quotes: Project narratives = 'coherent, performative narratives that project an intended future' (p. 44).
coding_notes: Complements Ika (2025) and Dille (2018) on the temporal-machinery side.

definition: No governance definition. Cooperation (Calamel et al.): 'the stance or attitude of members... their willingness (or reluctance) to work together' (p. 872).
stakeholders: 16 partners; no hierarchical decider; cooperation oscillates.
temporality_detail: Moderate. Three sequences; pace clash (p. 880). No electoral time.
misalignment_detail: Temporary-permanent coupling; the 'permanent context' could be the government-of-the-day.
gaps: Coupling lens transferable; no political clock.
key_quotes: Cooperation = 'the stance or attitude of members... their willingness (or reluctance) to work together' (Calamel et al., p. 872).
coding_notes: Temporary-permanent coupling is a useful analogue for project-vs-government-of-the-day.

authors: Emma Bourne, Marian Bosch-Rekveldt, Ossi Pesämaa
outlet: International Journal of Project Management 41, art. 102486
definition: Governance = 'the system of controls that suggest an overall direction for the project... matching activities, goals, intentions and performance' (p. 2). Müller (2009): 'a subset of corporate governance... value system, responsibilities, accountabilities, ethical principles, and policies.'
elements: six systemic errors (design, experience, bias, phase change, drift, intervention)
stakeholders: Client, contractor, public reps, steering committee; conflict from misaligned governance levels/mandates.
temporality_detail: Core & RQ-pointed. 'changes in technology, environmental factors and political pressures will happen over the life of the megaproject' (p. 8); 'drift' = context changes, governance does not adapt.
megaproject_detail: Windfarm 24 yrs; road; UK govt 'national priority' hospital programme.
misalignment_detail: Best model of governance that must move over long duration; six systemic errors ready-made for electoral-misfit failures, but external clock is generic.
gaps: Specialising 'moving governance' to a recurring electoral clock is open work.
key_quotes: Governance = 'the system of controls that suggest an overall direction for the project... matching activities, goals, intentions and performance' (p. 2).
'changes in technology, environmental factors and political pressures will happen over the life of the megaproject' (p. 8).
coding_notes: The pivotal moving-governance theory; six systemic errors are a candidate coding scheme for the thesis.

geography_sector: megaprojects as wicked policy fields; multi-level govt
definition: Megaprojects as wicked policy fields (complexity/uncertainty/conflict, p. 131); 'socioeconomic logic of megaproject governance' vs 'techno-economic... management' (p. 138).
elements: six complexity types incl. political-administrative (multiple governments)
stakeholders: Managers, policy-makers, citizens, movements; conflict can 'stop, suspend, delay, or amend' (p. 138).
temporality_detail: Moderate. 'megaprojects may take many years... how actors perceive the future is crucial' (p. 137); linear vs complex policy time; 'changes in political commitment.'
misalignment_detail: Nonlinear policy-process framing where conflict can 'delay... or amend'; electoral clock not modelled.
gaps: Policy-time framing; no explicit electoral cycle.
key_quotes: Conflict can 'stop, suspend, delay, or amend' a megaproject (p. 138).
'megaprojects may take many years... how actors perceive the future is crucial' (p. 137).
coding_notes: Extends Sanderson (2012); six-complexity typology parallels Qiu (2019).

authors: Raj Pathak, Neil Turner, Leila Alinaghian
method: systematic literature review (4,536->81 papers; Gioia method)
definition: Turner (2006): governance 'provides the structure through which the objectives of the project are set, the means of attaining those objectives... and the means of monitoring performance are determined'; APM (2019, p. 212): 'the framework of authority and accountability that defines and controls outputs, outcomes and benefits.'
elements: mechanisms (formal: alliance, process/institutional framework, contract, assurance/governmental, goal-alignment; informal: network, trust, relationship mgmt)
stakeholders: Multi-party; owner/client, governments, contractors, suppliers; 'no actor has total control and authority over all others' (von Danwitz).
temporality_detail: Moderate. Governance 'is regarded as dynamic, processual and anchored in multiple levels' (Abstract); evolutionary governance - 'governance issues as being static, but project development processes and environments are dynamic... governance regimes must adapt... and change as the project development process unfolds' (p. 9). No electoral cycle.
megaproject_detail: Systematic review of megaproject governance; inter-org core.
misalignment_detail: Names multi-level & evolutionary governance and future-research topics (governance at different levels; IPD (mis)alignment) - but no electoral/temporal-misalignment agenda.
gaps: Field-level confirmation of multi-level + evolutionary governance; no electoral-temporal agenda named.
key_quotes: Governance 'is regarded as dynamic, processual and anchored in multiple levels' (Abstract).
'governance regimes must adapt... and change as the project development process unfolds' (Miller & Hobbs, via p. 9).
coding_notes: Cites items 5, 6, 12, 13, 15 in this corpus - a citation hub. Neil Turner distinct from Rodney Turner (item 14).

authors: Christine Unterhitzenberger, Ralf Müller, Anne Live Vaagaasar, Yongjian Ke et al.
definition: Governance = 'the framework that outlines the boundaries for management's execution of their tasks and what they will be held accountable for' (Müller 2019); 'rules, relationships, systems, and processes for exercising... authority' (p. 88).
elements: three levels: metagovernance / governance of networks / network governance
metagovernance set by 'public government organizations or private large-scale investors'
stakeholders: Sponsor/owner/investor set metagovernance; prime contractor, subcontractors, delivery partners; accountabilities/responsibilities.
temporality_detail: Moderate. 'governance over time'; networks 'evolve throughout the project life cycle'; metagovernance 'allows for continuous adaptation... over time.' No electoral cycle.
misalignment_detail: Metagovernance 'set by... public government organizations' - the exact top layer an electoral change perturbs. Model directly usable.
gaps: The vertical stack localises where an election bites; electoral clock not modelled.
key_quotes: Governance = 'the framework that outlines the boundaries for management's execution of their tasks and what they will be held accountable for' (Müller 2019, p. 88).
Metagovernance is 'set by the owner or investor,' incl. 'public government organizations' (pp. 88-89).
coding_notes: The three-level stack is a primary structural tool for the thesis; Müller author cluster (items 2,7,22).

authors: Tammy E. Beck, Stephanie Solansky, Judith Davis, Karen Ford-Eickhoff, Donde Ashmos Plowman
method: case study; dynamic decision-making via modeling
definition: No governance definition. Boundary work = 'purposeful... effort to influence the social, symbolic, material or temporal boundaries' (p. 4).
stakeholders: 120+ agencies; deference to expertise + twice-daily meetings; shared boundary object resolves conflict.
temporality_detail: Moderate. Explicit temporal boundaries ('time, speed, and sequencing,' p. 3); trichordal sensemaking. No cyclical/electoral time.
misalignment_detail: Inter-org coordination + temporal-boundary + boundary-object lens. Peripheral to elections.
gaps: Temporal-boundary concept transferable; no political clock.
key_quotes: Boundary work = 'purposeful... effort to influence the social, symbolic, material or temporal boundaries' (p. 4).
coding_notes: Plowman links to Beck & Plowman institutional-emergence lineage.

authors: Ovie Afieroho, Yongkui Li, Yilong Han, Mladen Radujković
method: design-science research; two design principles (Lekki-Epe PPP, Nigeria)
definition: Governmentality lens: government strategies to 'shape, normalize, and instrumentalize the conduct and thoughts of others' (Rose & Miller); meta-organizing & responsibilization.
elements: meta-governance ('coordination of... governance modes... to overcome governance failures')
stakeholders: Government as dominant/steering stakeholder; private concessionaire; community. Conflict = community opposition/protests -> govt buy-out.
temporality_detail: Moderate & RQ-pointed. 'it took over two years to secure a sovereign guarantee... because the federal and state governments were controlled by different political parties at the time' (p. 5); govt actors seek 'political mileage for the next election' (p. 5).
megaproject_detail: PPP urban megaproject; Lekki-Epe, 30-yr concession; multi-level federal/state/local.
misalignment_detail: Empirically shows partisan misalignment across government levels delaying a megaproject two years - through governmentality/community-engagement, not a cyclical model.
gaps: Cross-level partisan delay shown; no cyclical electoral model.
key_quotes: 'it took over two years to secure a sovereign guarantee from the federal government because the federal and state governments were controlled by different political parties at the time' (p. 5).
Govt actors seek 'political mileage for the next election' (p. 5).
coding_notes: Governmentality lens shared with Turner (2020). Clearest cross-level partisan-delay evidence.

definition: Governance framework (Klakegg et al., 2008: S30) treated as public policy; neo-institutionalism (Scott's three pillars).
stakeholders: Treasury Board, deputy heads, project leaders, SDO, sponsor, Cabinet; actors added/removed each iteration.
decision_making: Yes - process tracing across five iterations.
temporality_detail: Core & RQ-critical. Five governance-framework iterations 1978-present mapped to changes of government (Liberal->Conservative->Liberal->Conservative->Liberal, Table 1); 'following the changes in the government parties, there have been... critical junctures... changes in vision and values' (p. 84).
misalignment_detail: Strongest demonstration that governance frameworks evolve with electoral/political alternation over decades - but framed as institutional layering/path dependency, not misalignment with a single project's timeline.
gaps: Framework-level (not single-project) trajectory; scale down to one megaproject crossing cycles.
key_quotes: 'following the changes in the government parties, there have been... critical junctures... changes in vision and values explicitly endorsed' (p. 84).
coding_notes: Same lead author as item 16 (Brunet 2021), distinct paper; shares Klakegg definition. Closest existing work to the RQ at framework scale.

authors: Javad Bakhshi, Petr Matous, Lynn Crawford
method: systematic review of 636 articles; bibliographic coupling
geography_sector: project governance (global corpus; megaprojects, PPPs, networks)
definition: PMI (2021): PG = 'guidance of project activities through frameworks, processes, and functions aligned with strategic, organizational, and operational objectives.' Müller (2016): controls / processes / relationships.
stakeholders: Principals/agents, stakeholders, networks across levels; conflict theorised per lens.
temporality_detail: Flags temporal governance as a gap. 'opportunities to explore temporal governance... how time-sensitive adaptations (e.g., to market or regulatory changes) impact project viability' (p. 11); 'sociopolitical changes as critical triggers for governance adaptations... often inadequately addressed.'
misalignment_detail: Field-level confirmation that temporal & sociopolitical-trigger governance is under-theorised - precisely the thesis's space.
gaps: Names the missing agenda (temporal governance; sociopolitical triggers) without filling it.
key_quotes: 'opportunities to explore temporal governance... how time-sensitive adaptations (e.g., to market or regulatory changes) impact project viability' (p. 11).
coding_notes: Most authoritative recent field map; legitimizes the thesis gap statement.

geography_sector: UK/USA/Germany/Canada; HS2, California HSR, Berlin Brandenburg, Trans Mountain
definition: No PG definition. Governance trap = mismatch between law-mandated stakeholder inclusion and shareholder-centric investment decisions (p. 6).
elements: 2x2 framework (mandated stakeholder inclusion x shareholder-centric investment)
Unified Governance / Mandated Stakeholderism / Voluntary Stakeholderism / Institutionalized Inclusivity
stakeholders: Managers, stakeholders (communities/third parties), shareholders/investors; 'stakeholders can leverage their legal rights to delay projects' (p. 6); conflict = protracted bargaining, project stalls.
temporality_detail: Moderate & RQ-relevant. Planning-stage cost growth + political funding pulls; 'protracted bargaining cycles' (p. 7); regime contrast - HSR 'progressed rapidly in authoritarian regimes' while liberal democracies delay (p. 6). Not a cyclical electoral model.
megaproject_detail: HS2; California HSR; Berlin Brandenburg; Trans Mountain.
misalignment_detail: Adds a political-decision-reversal instance (Sunak cancels HS2 phase 2, 'The facts have changed,' p. 6) and a democracy-vs-authoritarian tempo contrast. Frames delay as stakeholder-bargaining, not electoral entrainment.
gaps: Governance-trap 2x2 is a ready mechanism to which the electoral clock can be added.
key_quotes: PM Sunak justified cancelling HS2 phase 2 by declaring, 'The facts have changed' (p. 6).
'stakeholders can leverage their legal rights to delay projects' (p. 6).
coding_notes: Reuses the shareholder/stakeholder axis from Joslin & Müller (2016). Strong megaproject + political-system framing.

authors: Lavagnon A. Ika, Jonas Söderlund, Jeffrey K. Pinto
definition: No governance definition. Temporary org = 'a set of organizational actors working together on a complex task over a limited period of time' (Bakker 2010, p. 468).
stakeholders: Divergent horizons: 'project managers... short-term concern... project funders... longer-term perspective' (p. 2).
temporality_detail: Core (dedicated temporality theory). Entrainment = 'temporal fit between project activities and temporal demands imposed by the external environment' (pp. 5-6, incl. 'politics, government regulations'); manager-vs-funder horizons (p. 2).
megaproject_detail: Notes megaprojects 'blur the boundaries between temporary and permanent' (p. 3).
misalignment_detail: The conceptual engine - names entrainment/misfit incl. politics/government - but never instantiates the electoral cycle.
gaps: Treat the electoral cycle as a zeitgeber the megaproject fails to entrain to.
key_quotes: Entrainment = 'a process of establishing temporal fit between project activities and temporal demands imposed by the external environment (e.g., events)' (pp. 5-6).
'project managers... short-term concern... project funders... longer-term perspective' (p. 2).
coding_notes: Söderlund co-authors Dille (2018) and Ika (2025) - the temporal-theory spine of the corpus. Duplicate upload (e62d7f41) not counted.

method: typology of political resistance; 30 interviews + 50 press articles
definition: No PG definition - energy-transition governance & local political agency in a multi-level (unitary French) system (p. 1).
stakeholders: Local elected officials as political mediators who 'interpret, mediate, and sometimes amplify' opposition (p. 6).
temporality_detail: Core & explicitly electoral (keystone). NIMEY; 'electoral mandates are short-lived. This temporal misalignment reinforces both NIMEY and NIMTOO behaviours' (p. 6).
megaproject_detail: Inter-org/multi-level core; large infrastructure, not $1bn megaproject.
misalignment_detail: Empirical instantiation of the RQ's mechanism for local officials & renewable-energy projects. Remaining gap: scale to megaproject governance with multiple electoral turnovers per project.
gaps: Names the exact mechanism (electoral misalignment) but at local-official / non-megaproject scale.
key_quotes: 'The benefits of energy transition programmes generally materialise in the medium to long term, whereas electoral mandates are short-lived. This temporal misalignment reinforces both NIMEY and NIMTOO behaviours' (p. 6).
Local officials 'interpret, mediate, and sometimes amplify' opposition (p. 6).
coding_notes: The single closest template (NIMEY/NIMTOO) to the thesis's construct; built for local politics, to be scaled up.
